review: I just enjoy the game. I play solo. At 64 years old I can't keep up with the younger players on an online server. I play for relaxation.

A few years ago this would've been a positive review. Every time I pick this game up I find out that the devs have remade some important part of the game (building system, combat system, thrall system, journey system) and have made a bunch of minor changes or removals... and the bugs I remember from a few years ago are still there, sometimes along with new ones. 

Enemies are still sometimes disappearing after being killed or KOed, just like several years ago. An enemy will still sometimes step onto a rock and stop responding to anything. Fighting an enemy on terrain that isn't perfectly flat and targeting an enemy will sometimes make the camera shoot up to a bizarre angle that doesn't even let me see my character.  At least night exists again -- during the last age/chapter/whatever nighttime [i]stopped happening if you were in the southern part of the map[/i].

Funcom [i]really[/i] wants to make sure you look at their ads. A couple of days ago I even got a pop-up when starting the game that asked if they could collect data from me in order to see how well their advertising was working.
The company has decided to make you run the game through their own launcher now (which means they can push more stuff at you).
The game now has an in-game cash shop with a premium currency (Crom Coins). You earn "challenge exp" by doing randomly-assigned tasks, which unlocks special cosmetic items, except [i]not really[/i] in most cases because you need to buy a "battle pass" to actually get access to most of them.
The game effectively has ads for another game (Conan Chop-Chop) embedded in it in the form of figurines. You can decide not to make them, but they're going to be there in your crafting knowledge list. They're in mine, at least, and I didn't put them there.

The old journey system which let you finish things in any order you wanted and get rewarded with exp has been replaced with dozens of individual "journeys" with steps that have to be done in a specific order. This doesn't sound too bad at first, until you realize that requiring an order for some of them makes no sense, and that you can only progress one "journey" at a time. [b]Is it really a bad thing that I wanted to put on pants and shoes BEFORE doing anything else, Funcom?[/b]
The old journey system was something that you could use as a guide, but it never felt like it got in your way or made you do things a certain way -- "Hm. Have I finished everything in this area? The journey guide says there's something called the Tower of Bats that I can climb. I'll go check that out." The new one feels like being given orders by someone with OCD (and then being handed a box as a reward, which turns into two hundred plants that trap you under their weight when you open it, if you don't know what to expect). I get that they were probably trying to give more focused tutorials for specific parts of the game, but the implementation is [i]bad[/i] and messes with natural exploration and progression.
Well, you can just ignore it... right? There [i]is[/i] a gameplay option for turning it off... except that [b]some of the crafting blueprints are locked behind journeys[/b].

Speaking of progression, early-game enemies now drop mid-game gear. As far as I can tell, the only reason to craft an iron sword or a hunting bow now is because one of the "journeys" tells you to. You can get multiple copies of better gear from river or desert exiles (damaged, but you'll also have weapon repair kits), and the droprate is [i]high[/i]. If it were a rare thing, it would feel cool and you'd feel lucky for getting it, but now it just feels like they want everyone to rush through the early game as quickly as possible. Just like the in-game shop and the "battlepass", it's the type of thing you'd expect to see in a dying MMO, not a survival game.

tl;dr -- Game used to be good but the company kept messing with it, pushing ads, pushing in-game purchases, and failing to fix glaring bugs.

I've liked this game from the start (I started playing during the first month of Early Access). The mood and atmosphere really suited me, even though I have little to none experience with the conan universe. Also I generally like open world survival games. I came to Conan from countless hours of Ark: Survival Evolved, and although they have many similarities, this is an entirely different game.

Conan Exiles have had its ups and downs. There has been a LOT of server issues and game bugs, and much of the game mechanics has been revamped several times, such as combat. There has also been some trouble with the developers interraction with the community, but this have improved a lot.

When the game first came out, it didn't have that much to offer to the survival genre that we hadn't already seen in similar games, except maybe the avatars, large deity-based creatures that can be summonned at endgame to really wreck havoc on other players. Sadly, this was very overpowered, and the game got boring really quick. The gameplay (for me at least) was mostly Farming -> Building -> Get raided -> Repeat.. But as I said, the mood and atmosphere in this game made it bearable none the less. And sometimes I would just explore, and each time I would find something new, like a new NPC camp, friendly NPC's that would teach you stuff, some kind of lore (that is scattered around the entire map), caves/dungeons, etc.

The leveling and combat was boring at first, it was mostly just spamming the attack-button on buggy creatures while running around, or shoot the more powerful creatures from a safe place. But this was not a big problem for me, I enjoyed the game anyways. My biggest issue at that time was how easy it was to exploit the game and the mechanics, and the PvP was very unsatisfying. It was more or less required to build your base up high on mountains and such, then remove all the stairs so you couldnt get raided. The whole ordeal was just stupid and sad, and the game couldnt be played the way it was meant to be.

After a couple 100 hours I took a long break from the game. I hadn't played through any of the dungeons since I mostly played alone, but I reached max lvl and felt like i had seen the most of what the game had to offer.

And now, many months later, I am back.

At first it felt like the same game I had played before, except for a more cinematic intro, and a bit improved Character Creation. But it didnt take long before this felt almost like a new game for me!

The combat feels much more alive now with more dynamic combos and movements. Enemies are WAY less bugged, and they all have their own patterns which is similar to games like Dark Souls. Combat now includes things like lock-on and enemy health bar, which is very satisfying for me. I haven't tried archery yet, which was my primary fighting method when I first played this game, but I hope I will see improvements there as well.

When it comes to the world in general the map has gotten so much bigger, with two new biomes! Also old familiar places have been pimped up, and the world seems even more lively now. And still, the game is more performance-friendly then ever!

When it comes to PvP I've seen a lot of improvements, such as traps for raid protection, counter measures for the avatars, time window for Structure Damage, etc. The combat is also more dynamic now (you can defeat a player even when you have weaker weapons and lower lvl, if you know what you're doing). This opens up for building more freely, which is a very important aspect for me! Also I feel the community recently has become more friendly (even in Europe, haha).

And then we have the building/crafting aspect, which I've always liked in Conan (compared to games like Ark). This have also been greatly modified/improved. There are so many things you can craft, and for the architects out there, there is few limitations when it comes to structures and building. Also, the new system of which you learn the different crafts is so satisfying (for me at least), even though it took some time to get used to.

And last, when you're not building or engaging in PvP, the gameplay revolves heavily around lore and dungeons. (this is maybe an even more important aspect in PvE). And there is just so much to explore!

Conclusion: Though the game still has bugs (a few which I find severe) I really see a lot of improvements in an already good game, and I cant wait for the release!

The only negative thing I have to say right now is that the plans for mounts and magic is scrapped (for now atleast), and i was SO looking forward to that! :(

Hope this was helpful!

Cheers! :)

I've spent quite a few hours in Conan Exiles - mostly in single-player because there are quite a few issues with the bugs in the game that have NEVER been addressed - one of which is connecting to servers. It's hard to get friends into the game when the game itself just randomly tells you it can't connect. I have tried all the so-called 'fixes' for this [sometimes i'm successful sometimes I'm not] but it's an issue that has been around for years now. Mostly this aspect of being unable to join servers lead me down the path of single-player and all the wonderful mods this community has put out over the years.

This is a survival adventure game with PvP elements. Survival Adventure has rarely been done with bosses and progression quite the same way before Conan Exiles. You have a list of in-game goals and achieving them grants you experience. Here's the thing; some of those goals are actually quite fun, and the ones that tell you to go after bosses [in the base map] are the best. The bosses in the base map can be quite a challenge to a single person and getting to them is quite a challenge on its own. They are fun, and they unlock better gear to go after tougher bosses. More than that they are integrated into the game in such a way that you actually have lore for these bosses. The care and diligence with the way the world building was taken made this game incredibly unique when it first launched.

PvP [Player versus Player]. Full disclaimer; I don’t engage with PvP in survival games. If you like PvP I can’t recommend this game to you because Funcom doesn’t know how to support you. You don’t have to take my word for it, just google “Everything wrong with Conan Exiles PVP” from Ceronesthes [a pvp veteran], for a whole host of issues [and potential fixes] Funcom refuses to consider when balancing the game for PvP.

[Isle of Siptah] The first expansion; when initially brought to PC, it was so devoid of content their main player base Player vs. Enemy [PvE] camp had nothing to latch onto in the map. The Isle of Siptah has a number of issues - chiefly it being pay-to-win in PvP [there are items/armor on this DLC map you can't get on the base map]. Which is fine - it's a design choice Funcom made - but it's a choice that made a lot of players upset. And it didn't help the ailing PvP community at all. 

After they revamped the Isle of Siptah map HEAVILY did it even become playable in single player - but it's still a map that feels like it didn't have the same care an attention put into it like the base game. Some of these bosses can be fun, but they aren’t ingrained into the map in the same way as the base map through gameplay/ lore/ and straight up world building. They took one of the most unique and fun things about their game and put zero effort in that regard on their first expansion.

Modders are fixing the game and adding the content the player base was begging for.  If it weren’t for the modders this game would have had a much shorter life cycle. Not enough credit or love is going to the small community churning out FREE content.

TLDR: Microtransactions becoming more and more aggressive as time goes on

[i]I'll get this out of the way before I even start. I am going to compare this game to ARK and Rust. While it is its own beast with its own merits and flaws, it is within the same genre, and many people will wonder how it compares in certain aspects.[/i]

Out of every early access survival game, Conan Exiles has the most potential I've ever seen, and it's the first day. I am completely baffled by the negative response. Compared to ARK at its release, this game has a much clearer vision and a more complete framework; even if a lot of the contents of that framework are missing or buggy. I'm inclined to believe the negative reception is due to the fact that Conan is an existing IP, not a new one. People might just expect an IP like this to be complete, and not release in Early Access. I'm not entirely sure why those people purchased the game in the first place. There is definitely a bright blue EARLY ACCESS banner on the Steam store page.

All that said, the game does have a lot of issues. There's a lot of seemingly random framedrops, even to the point of the game completely freezing for several seconds. I'm confident this will be worked out with further optimisation, but it is an issue that has somewhat affected my enjoyment of the game.

[u]Pros[/u]
[list][*][b]Customisation[/b] - [i]By far the best character creation I've seen in a survival game. It's nearly at proper RPG levels.[/i]
[*][b]Presentation[/b] - [i]The presentation and atmosphere of the game, at least initially is superb. I can only suspect that it will get better from here.[/i]
[*][b]User Interface[/b] - [i]Best UI in its genre. It's simple, but not ARK simple. I said simple, not ugly.[/i]
[*][b]Graphics[/b] - [i]The game isn't the absolute [b]best[/b] looking game in the genre, but it's obvious there was a lot of care put into the visuals.[/i]
[*][b]Mining[/b] - [i]Definitely the most interesting and satisfying mining system I've seen so far. The rocks dent and chunk away in the place you hit them before finally crumbling. It's a minor thing, but it's pretty nice.[/i]
[*][b]Leveling and Crafting[/b] - [i]Fairly similar to ARK, but a bit more streamlined in my opinion. As you level up you gain points to level up attributes like Strength or Encumbrance. Furthermore you gain points to purchase crafting recipes. But unlike in ARK, a lot of the recipes in Exiles will net you two or more items.[/i][/list]

[u]Not Bad, But Definite Room For Improvement[/u]
[list][*][b]Combat[/b] - [i]As you get better armour and weapons, combat becomes much much better. There is a degree of "Git gud" going on. However, blocking responsiveness isn't fantastic, and enemy range isn't always what you'd expect it to be.[/i]
[*][b]Building[/b] - [i]Exiles is in an interesting spot of having a building system that is very similar to ARK's, but also better. The size of the individual building pieces is rather small, but despite this, you don't feel like a giant standing in a hobbit hole if you only build your shelter one wall high. Looking at you here, ARK.[/i][/list]

[u]Cons[/u]
[list][*][b]General Bugginess[/b] - [i]Very buggy, but not so much that it's unplayable.[/i]
[*][b]Optimisation[/b] - [i]Not very well optimised, but it is still much better than similar games at their launch.[/i]
[*][b]Co-Op Desync Bugs[/b] - [i]Haven't tested server multiplayer, but Co-Op, even with a good connection has lots of desync issues. Time of day isn't always going to match up between players. I was also—as the person not hosting—randomly losing my tools as I tried to equip them. At one point we also saw two different items in the same slot of a chest. Removing the item and dropping it reverted it to normal.[/i]
[*][b]Spawning[/b] - [i]This is mainly an issue for animals, but it's also somewhat problematic for players too. Animals will frequently spawn right on top of you. Out of the time I've spent playing, no less than 3 crocodile-alligators made my ballsack their personal spawnpoint. Of course, I could have been in the wrong place at the wrong time, but it seemed a bit too coincidental. This exacerbates the issue with low level beds. When you're low enough level that you are having trouble with a single croc, having another spawn on you means nearly certain death. I haven't unlocked beds yet, but I'm assuming they're more than single use, as the low level bedrolls break after one respawn. I feel like this is kind of counter productive. All it does is encourage resource wasting by building 2+ bedrolls and filling your base with them. Cut trees, gather stone, survive the weather, build your base, upgrade your gear, capture thralls, clear dungeons, kill bosses, and just try to stay alive in this massive world. Conan really nails that survival sandbox feeling for me.

As I push 200 hours I feel it is time to give a competent review of "Conan Exiles" in its current state, and from my perspective given the style and game mode we (my wife and I) are currently playing. Just a note, we are diehard Conan fans, and the given genre is right in our sweet spot having been avid "AD&D" and "Everquest" players back in the day.

I have at least tried most of the popular survival games on the market, taking far greater interest in games such as "The Forest" and "Empyrion" than games such as "Ark" which I played some, and games like "Rust", "Life is Feudal", "Day Z", "7 D2D", which I sampled but never really got into. I also greatly enjoy many of the single player survival games some of which are VR capable such as "Subnautica". While I consider myself equally PVE and PVP centric as a player, playing ARK PVP was nothing short of a relentless and unproductive experience and despite some tenacious efforts to enjoy it on my part, was never fun to play. However “ARK” in VR is nothing short of one of the greatest treats I have ever encountered as a lifelong gamer of many years. 

Up until "Conan Exiles" we have just been kicking around with games like "Overwatch", and beta testing "Shroud of the Avatar", "Gloria Victis", "Savage Lands" etc... We have also basically played just about every MMO on the market including "Conan" for many years. I would say we have extremely discerning taste when it comes to gaming and will happily take a quality game like "Mount and Blade" whose lack of graphics are easily made up for with content and replay ability. 

This is the perspective with which I am judging "Conan Exiles" understanding that it is still in EA and continues to evolve to a finished product. I would also recommend paying little heed to any reviews be they positive or negative from any "testers" who have not put at least 10 to 20 hours into the game due to the complexity of the in game systems and the sheer time it takes to experience various aspects of the game short of drastically altering the default settings. Conversely I'd caution against listening to the people who play with x10 everything and then complain that the game is too easy and lacking in content. So is the Rubik’s Cube if you physically take it apart and reassemble it correctly.

As much as we have wanted to continue playing on the official PVP servers, the experience was tantamount to that which we had in "ARK" in that when you aren't fighting relentless server issues, you are contending with a completely unbalanced, often toxic population of people hell bent on making your in game experience anything but productive or pleasurable by utilizing the plethora of bugs, glitches and exploits which currently riddle the PVP portion of the game. I am confident that in time, given the tenacity of the devs and their constant efforts to patch and improve the game, that these issues will become manageable and we will revisit that element of the game in the future. In the meantime the two of us are just playing PVE together on a private server, and truth be told, we are absolutely loving the game. In fact, from this perspective, there is little to nothing, save some minor bugs here and there that we even dislike about the game.
It has been somewhat similar from a survival and crafting point of view to our coop experience in "The Forest" and "Empyrion", albeit even simpler to learn and progress than in either of those games. We have only slightly deviated from the default settings and are taking our time progressing through the content. We are both around level 30 and have tried to balance our time between building, leveling and exploring, all of which are extremely rewarding in their own way.

Graphically the game is phenomenal and runs beautifully on our rigs, both of which are powerful machines.
The grind is definitely present but is by no means as laborious as many games of the genre, and by comparison is in some ways more straight forward and rewarding.

There is no shortage of flora and fauna, as well as recipes and uses for that which you obtain from harvesting them. If anything, the fauna can be a bit overwhelming in the earlier stages of the game and act as kind of a meter suggesting by one's success or failure if it is time to move on, or to stay put and improve gear and attributes a bit more.

My wife and I are always on the hunt for games that we can play together be they MMOs, survival or tower defense genres. We dabble with the "Dark Souls" series, but "Conan Exiles" truly satisfied just about every aspect of our gaming needs. Most importantly, we are having fun playing in a way so many games simply fail to deliver.
There will definitely come a time when we will yearn to play this game in a PVP setting, but currently we are enjoying the aspect of the game we are playing and the experience is nothing short of a 10/10 for us.

I would surmise that the best way to appreciate this game in a PVP setting would be on a limited and well modded server of maybe twenty to thirty people or so, with smaller clan size limits of perhaps five people per clan. Obviously the more like minded the players are on the server, the more enjoyable the experience will be for everyone. Alas, not everyone has ten or twenty friends they can get to play the same game, but this is one game which would truly shine above most given such a scenario. We definitely look forward to the server issues being improved, and we remain encouraged by the obvious care and time the devs are continuously putting into the game's development. Until then we will continue to enjoy this great experience and look forward for more to come as the game progresses.

I'll swap this to a thumbs up if they finish the rest of the game.  The issue is you'll come across bugs that were reported in 2017, but have not been addressed.  Sometimes you'll see comments on the forum that they have plans to fix said issue(or that they have, when in truth they have not), other times no response.  Instead of fixing the gamebreaking issues, the developers are working on new features.  The fan boys will frequently give you suggestions on how to cope with the bug.  Do x and then y, and the bug should go away for a bit.  This is not acceptable, believe me, I develop software for a living.

Here are just a few major/medium issues:
-thralls(think of this as a D2 merc that follows you) will not attack until either you attack, get hit, or they are hit.
-thralls randomly decide they will do nothing but stand there, even while being killed.
-thralls that finally decide to attack, will randomly pick a passive enemy not even in range, and run to it to pull it into the fray.  Sometimes the enemy will sit there taking no damage, all while your thrall continues hitting it.  You have to walk within a certain distance for the game to decide to deal damage to said target.  Doing so, may pull additional enemies, and your thrall will likely repeat the process of finding a passive enemy to aggro.
-thralls with melee weapons miss anything that slightly moves.  Are you being chased?  Don't worry, derpy will swing his/her weapon at the wind.  You have to time it just right so that w/e derpy is swinging at isn't moving at the time of the swing.
-thralls with bows, randomly just decide they will never shoot another arrow

-purge, first 3 waves spawned directly outside base, as they should.  Remaining waves spawned on top of base and did major damage.  Our base was perfectly exposed for pathing, but nope, purge was dropped directly on top of roof.  Last wave spawned Rockslide directly INSIDE the 1st floor.  We lost everything.  This was with T3 blocks.

-sometimes when looting your corpse, your items will not show up in your inventory.  You have to log out and back in for them to magically appear.

-players, thralls, enemies glitching through walls/floors.  Multiple times now I've almost killed a boss, only for it to fall through the floor or a wall, and never to be seen again, until server restarts.  I was even pulling a named volcano archer to my thrall wheel, and it glitched through the mountain.  It was never found.

-pets, especially greater ones have garbage stats compared to thralls.  There is no purpose to really have them outside of their poop, gold/silver dust, etc.

-chests that decide they'll never restock.  Went a few days without the rusted keys(for scrap armor chests) respawning.

-weapons that claims to ignore armor, but do not.  2handed axes(in name/description) that are actually 1handed axes.

-rng in this game is so utterly bad.  I spent a full week of trying to get snow hunter to spawn at 1% chance, only for her to spawn 9 out of 11 times in exact same spot.  Other examples include bosses continually dropping the exact same gear, until rng clicks over, and now they start magically dropping w/e it was they refused to drop before, time after time.  Pet rng for getting a variant or greater is so awful(yes i know about different foods influencing the odds).

-pretty often you'll pull off a perfect dodge, only for the game to teleport you back to where it thinks you got hit.  You don't get the stamina back and you take full damage.  It's an auto-death if you get stuck near a wall surrounded by undead or anything that can stagger/knock you down.  You'll roll, and appear to have gotten away, only to instant port back to wall cluster, and continue to be killed/locked.

-enemies from absurd range will just instant target the player.  This is a real pain when you're walking through an area with animals, and instantly you have king elk, wolves, mammoths, bears, etc coming at you at full force.  I remember that episode on the Discovery channel, where the elks decided to join forces with their number 1 enemies, to kill the humans(j/k).

-enemies sometimes even after sustaining well over 70% of their hp in damage from your thrall, will continue trying to kill you, even when you haven't attacked.

-the aoe graphics for clouds(corruption, noxious, etc), especially in the volcano and broken springs, frequently don't match hitboxes.  I've been walking through fire graphics taking no damage, and other times been randomly hit by corruption and noxious stacks, even when there is nothing in sight.  Another example is spiders and reapers often won't fire a projectile, but you'll get poison stacks.

-when building you have to place certain blocks/building pieces in a specific order, or they won't line up or snap together.  The gate is a great example.  

-Sometimes you'll get the "failed to place object."  When there is clearly no reason you can't place said building object.  The work around is to swap to another object, and then back to the one you had.  This is so annoying when building large bases.

things that aren't bugs but don't really make any sense to me:
-with friendly fire enabled, you can hit each other, including thralls.  Enemies do not hit each other.  This seems silly.  If a cluster of skeletons are body blocking you against the wall wildly swinging, they should be hitting each other too.
-this game sometimes plays like a souls game, and other times something else.  They need to decide what it is.
-enemy archers range from never able to hit you even when standing still, to able to auto-aim you even if you are sprinting, rolling, zig zagging, etc.  Sometimes they'll snipe you through trees.
-inability to lock storage containers.  I would like it if I could lock/code my own storage so that clan mates don't ninja or 'borrow' things that I need.
-There are lots of bugs in the game, that can only be resolved by restarting the server.  Again this is a work around, not a fix.  This should not be needed as much as it is.
-Xp tables feel very half-butted.  Imagine how annoying it is to kill the undead which are plentiful, high in hp, do not bleed/poison, and can't be stunned.  They give a few thousand xp.  Now imagine a ram, rock rocknose, etc that you can take out with 1 hit that gives large sums of xp.  Yes I can get to lv 60 fast, that isn't my issue with xp.  I need xp to level my thralls.

I never got the whole "survival game" craze. I find their design fascinating from a technical point of view, and I've enjoyed watching others stream them, but to me most look like slightly more edgy versions of Minecraft. Aside from this being a "controversial" game in a setting I already like, I might not have picked it up. So far, I'm glad I did.

This is an open world survival game in the Conan setting by Robert E. Howard. He was a friend and correspondent of H.P. Lovecraft, and they both drew inspiration from each other's work over the years. Lovecraft wrote about the "cosmic horror" of humanity's place in an uncaring universe haunted by forgotten abominations; Howard wrote of forgotten civilizations where the humans are the real monsters. Having found yourself on the wrong end of "civilized" justice is where your story begins.

Character creation starts with your new Exile crucified in the desert. You have the usual sliders to adjust facial features and so on, and more to adjust your height, muscle tone, and *ahem* endowment. Yes, there are boob and dong sliders. Yes, if you enable full nudity on your server, you can see it all in full detail, at least on characters without clothing equipped. Yes, of course people lost their minds over this. If you don't enjoy that sort of thing, it's easy enough to change and it's off by default. I made my Exile as big, buff, and buxom as her sliders would allow.

Once you're done with character creation, the opening scene shows Conan himself finding your doomed Exile. Crucifixion is barbaric even by his standards, so he cuts you down from the cross and gives you a second chance at the struggle for life, or at least a glorious death in battle. You'll be experiencing a lot of both.

You start naked in the desert on the edge of the Exiled Lands. Your worst enemies in the beginning are thirst, starvation, and the sun. And sandstorms, which will kill you faster than you can ask "what song is this?" if you don't find shelter in time. Fortunately, dying just sends you back to your spawn point with half your Health, and your inventory will still be on your body if you can find it before it eventually disappears. You can recover your stuff as many times as you're willing to retrace your steps to loot your own corpse, but sometimes you can't due to dying in a dangerous or inaccessible area. You can respawn at your bed or bedroll once you have them, and keeping spare gear stashed in your base is a good precaution.

Base building is pretty user-friendly. Once you've crafted an axe and/or pick from loose branches and rocks, you can cut wood and stone to assemble foundation blocks, walls, and ceilings. The trees grow back soon enough, and so do the rocks, as long as you haven't built anything over them. The things you can make are controlled by your Feats, and other structures like stairs are relatively cheap to unlock. Once you've placed your first part, new parts snap to each other in a grid pattern. You can't build too far out without support from a foundation block or the terrain. For example, unsupported staircases can only be three tiles high, so no stairway to heaven. (Denied!) Beyond that, the construction rules are pretty forgiving. You can build all the sandstone skyscrapers you want, and cover the Exiled Lands in affordable housing to your heart's content.

Some items you can craft by hand, others you need to craft equipment for, like a furnace to smelt Ironstone into Iron Bars. Most things like furnaces and campfires work like appliances: Put your ingredients in their inventory, click the Play button, and walk away to do other stuff. They stop automatically when they run out of materials or fuel. They have visual cues to tell you when they're working, like smoke rising from a campfire, and you can see their inventory at a passing glance without opening it. Their descriptions only hint at their most common use, so you should experiment to avoid missing out on useful combos. You could say I was searching for the Riddle of Steel, because it took me a week to figure out how to make any, despite having everything I needed. (I had overlooked some item descriptions which spelled it out.) Weapons, armor, and tools degrade with use, and you can only repair what you know how to make. A lot of supplies (like human flesh and other food) are perishable, but you can slow their decay by storing them in special containers. Structures decay over time, but the timer for this is lenient enough (at least in my normal difficulty solo game) that it rarely matters.

You can eventually build the Wheel of Pain, a place where you break captured Exiles and turn them into Thralls. Knocking out a non-player Exile with special weapons lets you bind them and drag them to the Wheel, and feed them as they work until they're ready to serve you. Assigning an artisan Thrall to some equipment makes crafting faster, and they might know recipes you don't. Fighting Thralls defend your base from wandering monsters and other Exiles, but you must feed them; a Thrall Pot can hold and preserve food for them. You can also adopt animals, like the baby turtles wandering the beach, and feed them until they grow into fearsome pets.

Crafting and harvesting slowly fill a Purge meter, which eventually results in waves of attackers invading your base. EDIT 11/22/2023: This mechanic has been completely reworked in the recent Age of War updates, and now requires deliberate action (hoarding special treasures in a vault) to trigger, making it fully optional.

Combat and exploration are both pretty smooth. You can climb almost anywhere, but some dungeons are no-climbing zones to keep you from bypassing puzzles. How far you can climb before losing your grip is controlled by your Stamina, as are jumping and sprinting, and (in combat) your attacks and dodge-rolling. When low, it refills in seconds if you walk, jog, or stand still. If you let it run out completely, it will take longer to refill, and you can't do anything that needs Stamina until it's full, which is bad news if it happens during a chase or fight. The only way to heal most of the time is to slowly regenerate Health by eating food, which stops if you get hit. No pausing time to chug instant healing potions or eat all the cheese, so you really need to avoid getting hurt, and it will take a while to nurse yourself back to full health after almost dying.

The open world is beautiful and full of interesting little secrets, and you may see ghosts from time to time, or touch strange monoliths that speak to you in your mind. Climb around the most treacherous terrain long enough, and you might find a treasure chest or a journal on a ledge halfway up a cliff.

Time flies when you're building sandcastles. I started with one tiny shack under Shattered Bridge to have somewhere to put my bedroll. The sign outside now reads "One Sandstone Plaza" to distinguish it from the rest of the complex, which dozens of thralls and pets call home.

TL;DR: Naked cannibal woman gentrifies Exiled Lands, rocks and trees hardest hit, would get crucified again.

Conan Exiles is a fantastic game ruined by a mix of questionable mechanics, imbalanced gameplay, and game breaking glitches. If you are thinking of getting the game I HIGHLY reccommend reading the game breaking glitches section first. Let's start with the questionable mechanics bit:

QUESTIONABLE MECHANICS: This section describes DECAY TIMERS, THRALLS, RAIDING, and EXPERIENCE/PROGRESSION

1.) There is a decay timer that will delete your buildings after a certain amount of time not using them. You need to stand next to a building for at least 10 mintues for the decay timer to go up a whole lousy hour. What if you want to take a break? Want a vacation? Well I hope you have enough time on the decay timer so the shit you spend several hours making and crafting don't just up and delete themselves so that the laggy servers don't lag more. Only way to circumvent this is to be on a private server with reliable and fair admins that are likely to keep the server running for a while (Maybe I'm just unlucky with private servers and admins being dicks?). 

2.) The THRALL TRAINING SYSTEM is cool and interesting, but the AI is so shit that it doesn't matter. Your horde of legendary thralls you spent days or weeks training sometimes don't even react to enemies, or will just try to fight them with their fists despite having weapons. I've had an elephant run into a small army of about 40 of my thralls, with only 4-6 of them reacting to the elephant's pressence. Players can easily systematically slaughter any number of thralls with just iron tools at their disposal. 

3.) RAIDING is extremely easy, whereas defending is near impossible without glitches. Stacking grease orbs and then throwing a single fire orb on top of the stacked grease orbs will cause the fire to do enough damage to break through any structure. If I spend 30 hours making the steel needed for tier 3 building materials for a fort with my buddies. Some random low level shouldn't be able to farm for 10 hours and break through that entire fort taking all of it's possessions. They put in windows for when people can raid you, but honestly I don't intend to be online for 6 hours every day just to watch my base. 

4.) PROGRESSION is very slow. You can hit level 50 in 3 days if you play 12 hours a day and know exactly what you are doing, but these types of games have a lot of content and stuff to learn to be able to do that. You spend a bunch of time hitting max level (which is level 60) so that you can use the cool end game perks just to find out there are game breaking glitches that are being abused by 10 people on the server you play on. If you hop servers, then you have to spend all that time grinding back up again. If you play on a private server, then you are at the mercy of the admins to be just and fair to you and others. I've seen people I thought were totally reasonable as admins spawn undead dragons on people's bases for shits and giggles. Slow progression doesn't matter much to me, but it's a bit much

IMBALANCED GAMEPLAY: 

1.) SET is the most powerful avatar capable of oneshotting Tier 3 foundations. Every other avatar can not do that.

2.) The spear is capable of stunlocking opponents at a further range than any other weapon. This wouldn't be a problem if a full combo from a full strength build didn't kill anyone who isn't specced entirely into vitality. 

3.) Tier one siege equipment like the grease orb and fire orb combo is too strong. My tier 3 foundations shouldn't be destroyed by the comparatively small amount of resources it takes to make the grease and fire orbs. 

4.) Tier three siege equipment is too cheap. I can build a trebuchet to knock down anyone's base while they are offline at level 25. Level 60 and have a massive base on a plateau? Well unless you have a god bubble (something else that takes too long to make) you're fucked. 

5.) The PURGE mechanic sends a large group of AI controlled mobs at your base after you build up to a certain point. This is fine, except some of the mobs that can be sent at you are boss mobs with enough HP that you will break your iron weapons 10 times on them before you see their HP go down to half. They are unkillable, and ridiculously overpowered. If they get to your base, the whole thing will be wiped without extensive preparations. This doesn't always happen, as sometimes the purge is weak as shit, but it's lame.

GAME BREAKING GLITCHES: Server lag, stat glitches, duplication glitches, and more.

1.) Official servers are garbage when they approach max capacity. Server states I should have a ping of 40 when I join the server, I get online and will have very small ping with few players online. When Raid time comes around (the set window the game allows for players on the official PVP server to raid each other) everyone logs on and the server FPS drops to 10. Ping spikes up and PVP becomes unplayable, NPCS get extremely glitchy and will stand instantly after being knocked down.

****EDIT**** I've been told that 2.) and 3.) in this section have been fixed. 

2.) There is a glitch that allows players to have 999 skill points. It's ridiculously unfair to fight people who abuse this without also abusing it yourself. You can only max one stat, with that glitch they can be 50/60 points into every stat where you can only get 60/60 in one. 

3.) THE WORST GLITCH OF ALL. There is a nasty duplication glitch that allows you to duplicate items in your inventory. It's terrible and game breaking. Get one dragonpowder, then duplicate duplicate duplicate until you have 4,000 of them and nobody wants to play anymore. 

OVERALL: Fun game, great building, decent rewarding combat, ruined by imbalanced gameplay and horrible bugs.  CURRENT STATE: 6/10

***EDIT***
This review is from the standpoint of someone who wanted the PVP experience and was sorely disapointed. Some people have mentioned that I failed to talk about the game from the PVE side of things: It's worse. Land claim griefing, which is placing objects near someone's base so that the other person can't build on the claimed land, is a big unfixable problem. Dragging mobs to houses to destroy them instead etc... 

The big point of playing on public servers is that the game should be fair and balanced, but it's not. exploits, glitches, griefing, and other forms of play not intended by the developers destroy my ability to enjoy this game. You can be banned on a whim by private server admins, or your favorite private server will get wiped, reset, or shutdown. Admins would get rid of cheaters and griefers, but are unreliable and very case specific. Answer should be to go to the public servers, but that comes with a whole new bucket of bullshit.

Too many problems for YOU to fix to enjoy the game. You can try to work around all the problems I've mentioned (and maybe you don't even care about some of them), but then you will just walk away with a bunch of mediocre compromises.

Once a year or so I get a craving for some survival game. I played mostly ARK and Conan Exiles when those moments occur and Conan Exiles is by far the superior title.

A thing to take in mind: I do not play these games multiplayer. I just wanna hop on, chop some trees, build some stuff and kill some stuff.

Why I recommend this game to people who just like to go on a solo adventure:
[list]
[*]Conan mythos. Plenty of well-established and intriguing lore that the game picks from. It's not shy on bringing the harsh world to digital life either with full on nudity and mentions of necrophilia and bestiality with of course buckets and buckets of blood and suffering.
[*] Combat. While not exactly Bayonetta or God of War, the combat is meaty and satisfying for a survival game that uses melee as its primary focus. Also lots of limbs and heads flying around.
[*] Game is pretty. And although it does have its performance quirks here and there, it's nowhere near as bad as ARK
[*] Building is intuitive, although of course the grind is real when you want to build something extravagant
[*] Purges (wave-based attacks by NPCs)
[*] Thrall system, where you can capture and eh... convince people to work for you.
[*] UI has some annoying things, but is mostly crisp and easy to navigate.
[*] Plenty of perks, buildings, weapons and armor to choose from
[*] Things that you can buy are only cosmetic, all gameplay systems and content is free
[*] You've got a full cheat interface at your disposal when playing alone, so if you just want to build stuff, you can go loco
[*] You can set the size of your character's penis
[/list]

Huge reminder: Conan Exiles is Funcom's most profitable game ever, by no small margin either. Yet it's still managed as it was in the Early Access days. Horrid client performance. Horrid server performance. Horrid modding capabilities (DLC is completely unmoddable, expanded upon below). Still limited to a 40/40 player cap for tolerable latency. AI is still brain-dead. Climbing is still janky and teleports you up/down/away from what you're climbing when you reach the top.

I'll expand on what's new, with my earlier criticisms being left as they are, as the faults are still as they were. And there's many of those.

Despite the game being advertised as moddable, that is only true for the base game. Modders are completely unable to modify the DLC in any way. We can't change the stats of DLC equipment. We can't distribute DLC equipment to NPCs. We can't change the recipes of DLC items. We can't modify the textures of DLC objects. We can't use the animations of DLC weapons. We can't do a damn thing to them. Bethesda, a company led by a banker that was banned from ever banking again, by the Federal Reserve for being corrupt, has a better DLC modding policy than Funcom. *Bethesda, of all developers.*

Performance is still embarrassingly awful, as the devs continue to not update to a newer version of UE4; there is no Vulkan support so even merely moderate bases tank the framerate with the beefiest CPU money can buy, as DirectX 11 has terrible draw call performance. A well-known example of this, outside of survival games, would be Fallout 4. When you build a settlement that just has a fitting amount of objects to actually look like a settlement, the draw calls climb into the tens of thousands, the framerate plummeting. Conan Exiles suffers the exact same issue.

Not only that, the entire game's scripting engine runs on a single thread, as Funcom has completely forgone the idea of backporting a freely available plugin on the marketplace that facilitates multithreaded blueprint scripts. Every single blueprint, which is used on everything from crafting stations, to NPC AI, to damage calculations, and everything in-between, are all being processed on a single thread.

Latency is still a major problem on servers with 30-40 players online, never mind the private servers that go above that. There are two causes for this horrible performance. The first being the aforementioned scripting system you'd expect from a game made in 2008. The latter, is that the databases are SQLite databases, which do not support multiple threads accessing them; only a single thread can access the entire database at one time. Those people are WRONG!
Conan Exiles gets a posive recommendation and I am going to explain why!

2. Technical review
Critized main issue: Server lagging/rubberbanding!
While it is true that - including for me - the game was simply unplayable in the first days of "Early Access" I keep being patient.
Why?

3. Game review
3.1 Character creation
3.2 Game concept
3.2.1 Combat
3.3.1 Thrall System
3.3.2 Religion

6. Conclusion


3.1 Character creation: 
You choose your sex, race, religion and customize your facial and body features with the help of sliders.
Due to the full nudity, you can enjoy resizing your characters dong to reflect what you wished for in reality or go all humble. Same counts for female breasts - Funcom tradition when thinking about Age of Conan.
However if you are prude there are options to disable or partially disable nudity.
I would never understand personally why someone might be offended from a naked human body but is totally fine with gore but ok, nevermind!
Facial hair for males are greyed out still, something that is going to change very fast surely.
The racial background is purely cosmetic and a roleplay aspect while religion has a deeper sense. More about this later.
Generally it feels very intuitive to create your character, not to overwhelming and not too simple and thankfully you can not create weird mutant like character like in ARK. You are Human and you are going to look like one - great!

3.2 Game Concept: 
Like many people already said before me, Conan Exiles does remind me the most of ARK. It uses the same engine (UE4) and the game concept is similar however in my opinion it feels like an updated version.
The menus are more intuitive and they also improved the building system because unlike ARK you can use the terrain, adapt the height of your foundations and build into mountainsides.
Sometimes certain parts do not want to snap in the right place but generally I prefer the Conan Exiles system over ARK, I had far less issues here.

So while generally being another survival game where you have to manage hunger, thirst, stamina, encumbrance and your health it brings new fresh elements into the genre (Soon more about it.)
I noticed a tiny nice feature regarding encumbrance. In other survival games you can freely move until you are encumbered - same goes for Conan Exiles - however the more you carry here, the less faster your Stamina regenerates which will decrease your intervals in which you are able to run!
Another survival aspect is "corruption"
The more time you spend with dark beings and dark places, you gain corruption which will overlap your health bar, effectively reducing your maximum available amount of health.
How to remove it? For this you need dancers! Yes, some nice men and women entertaining you! Read more about it later in the thrall section!
A neat little features!

3.2.1 Combat:
The combat system generally reminds me mostly of TES: Skyrim. Wield the weapons you want and attack your foes etc.
Nice but honestly I wish they will introduce a more in-depth system, currently you can try to dodge enemy attacks but it doesn't work intuitively yet and the possibility to cripple certain body parts is also missing.
You cannot hit someones arms so he cannot wield his weapon or cripple his legs so he cannot chase you e.g.
Shooting arrows at foes also doesn't bother them. They just keep running like they are made out of steel.
I hope they gonna change this however gore is a feature on s.o. death!

3.3.1 Thralls: 
A unique aspect of Conan Exiles is the feature that allows players to capture Human NPC's in order to break their will and make them work for you!
Some might think that it is similar to a pet system like ARK in which you tame dinosaurs but I think it is different and it also feels diferent in the game.
The possibility to tame and ride animals is not yet implemented in Conan Exiles but will come in the future, better reflecting the equivalency of taming dinosaurs in ARK probably.
The thrall system currently enables you to capture someone, bring him back to your camp and let him spin around in the hamster wheel - sorry -in the Wheel of Pain.
It takes quite some time but after the procedure is done you can make use of your new thrall.
However, they have certain qualities.
There are archers, fighters, blacksmiths, chefs, dancers and probably more.
There are NPC's with certain abilities out there which you have to find in order to fill in your desired role.
To remove corruption you will need dancers e.g.

3.2.2 Religion: 
A new and fresh aspect to the genre!
You choose the deity of your desire during character creation (currently there are four but they plan on bringing in more) and then you are able to build the first tier level of your deity's altar/shrine/etc.
Keep in mind that every deity is unique regarding items you can get but the mechanics are the same, you have to gain their favor!
There are two higher tiers of altars available (three in total, counting the starting one) with more unique religious items which you can unlock once you've reached higher levels!
When you gained the highest amount of favor, your deity will reward you be allowing you to summon his avatar which you can control then for a brief time (1 minute on default I think?) to crush everything in your path!
I am curious to see how much further they will develop the religious aspect!

4. Graphics:
I tried all the different graphics options, all the way from "low" to "ultra" and I can tell you that this game looks gorgeous, the graphics are very well done and manage to transfer an atmospheric feeling. Those sandstorms are gorgeous!
Something I could not test for myself yet required a low end laptop. In the graphics settings is a checkbox wich adapts the graphics specifically for low end laptops, enabling people with less sophisticated hardware to play the game.
The greatest atmospheric "turnoff" currently is the missing AI intelligence as well as NPC animations.

5. AI:
This is one of the priorities of the devs to change (Early Access) however currently, NPC's simply stand around, doing nothing and they feel rather robotic in their behavior and only get active when they spot to attack you.

6. Conclusion:
Fresh, new ideas for the survival genre! My main issues about rubberbanding or lack of AI intelligence and animations is subject to change, so I recommend the game!

At first, I was very sceptical about this game. But Conan could pleasantly surprise me. Please, remember that review is just an opinion, and I do not pretend for objectivity. Well...

I think that at launch this game was positioned wrong. I still remember these slogans: "Raid! Dominate! Become a power!", so it was easy to believe that Conan is a game about PvP. In fact, I did not find PvP in Conan interesting or exciting. I think, whole idea of such PvP and its mechanics are wrong in its core. Personally me would never agree to participate in contest when I need to spend multiple hours for creating some equipment, just to discover that everything I done was razed to ground while I was offline. I can not play for more than a couple hours per week, so I am totally useless in such "virtual wars of attrition".

By other side, PvE in Conan is wonderful. I mean - really. Game offers tons and tons of PvE content of very good quality. Me and three my friends played on private server and it was one of the most memorable, interesting and beautiful adventures I had. World of Conan is not an empty ground for building with resource nodes and monsters here and there. It is a fairly vast and gorgeously beautiful territory with different biomes, full of PvE encounters and, most importantly, filled with lore. This world has its own history to discover and learn, and I totally loved it. Most importantly, game rewards player for exploring, by visiting deeply hidden places you may find different valuable things - recipes for crafting, unique items, even new animations for your character.

Combat mechanics in Conan is fairly simple but decent. It is a fast hack-and-slash, mainly focused on melee and some ranged as support. The only one thing I disliked about combat is... some animations. I found it funny and even stupid when I stabbed a guy in leg with a spear... and suddenly head of this poor savage fell off his shoulders. In Conan, weird stuff happens with bodies constantly.

One of the main feaures of Conan - base building - is excellent. Game offers fairly large assortment of blocks and items you may construct with, and there is a huge space for player imagination and creativity. Well, just look at screenshots, look at all these wonderful temples, castles, whole cities... all of them were progected and constructed by players. Not to mention that game offers lots of decorative items - from banners and tapestries to ceramic pots and stuffed animals - so player may customise and decorate buildings with. And if basic sets are not enough for you - there are decorative DLC, which are adding even more items of different styles. Main flaw of base building system is that if there are too much objects, game may take a couple minutes to load and draw them. But it is a common problem of all similar games, as far as I know.

Mentioning decorative DLC again - they are totally unnecessary to purchase if you do not want to. DLC are just adding more different visual styles, all equipment such as armor and weapons have same stats as basic items, so they give no advantanges. Just pretty visuals, useful for roleplay.

As you finished your first shelter and gathered basic gear, you may try another important mechanics - capturing thralls. This is a vital part of game, as only thralls with advanced skills - blacksmiths, armorers, all sorts of craftsmen - will supply you with high-quality items. And so you will wander all around the map in search of NPC to enslave them and create your small army of obedient serfs. Eventually, you may gain a full escort of loyal bodyguards, docile servants and pretty dancers for pleasing your eyes.

Not only humans are available for capturing but also animals. Well, ironically, Conan is much more humane when it comes to pets. You need to beat a human to make him work for you, but you may find an animal cub - even a little crocodile - bring it into pen and feed it until pet grow. There is a nice diversity of animals in game so you may gather an impressive zoological collection if you wish.

Main thing you will be doing in PvE is exploring the ruins and fighting with bosses. While mechanics of bosses are not very original - many of them are just huge hard-hitting creatures with tons of health - still, boss-fights are tense enough and require some teamplay. And, as always, visual part is gorgeous.

Speaking about visual part, I must mention that I really liked models of characters. They are beautiful - as whole game in general. There is an optional full nudity in game but, if you do not want to see naked bodies, you may turn nudity off in game settings.

Game settings are fairly flexible, you may tweak and modify lots of important things such as speed of skill gaining and amount of gathered materials... so if you feel, for example, incomfortable with grinding resources, you may tweak it in game settings.

Important thing to mention is a fairly large amount of different modifications you may find in Conan community. For me, there are more than enough content in native game but, if you want... try to check modifications, there are some, well, weird stuff.

There are flaws in game, of course. First of all, I deeply missed any magic. I understand that by lore, world of Conan is a world from where magic is almost gone, leaving just some scattered remnants. By other hand, I really think that at least some magic, like summoning rituals or blessings and curses, could improve gameplay.

As for summoning so-called "avatar", I found it totally useless. It is a huge towering creature, impressive and powerful but clumsy, and it summoned for extremely limited time. I was impressed yet disappointed in same time. I thing that summoning in Conan has a lot of unreleased potential.

Another thing I missed is rideable creatures. So many times, travelling around the world of Conan, I thought about horse or camel or whatever creature I could ride. Unfortunately, game does not offer such mechanics.

Finally, I missed some sort of NPC mercenaries who could join player for payment. I mean - yeah, I may have thralls but why if I need services of particular character then I need to beat him until he fells unconscious? Why I just could not offer him some payment so he could join my settlement? Funny enough, there is a trading system, and sometimes you may even find NPC traders who may give you resourses in exchange for coins, but it is totally useless and whole potential of trading system is not even barely released.

Obviously, game is intended as a multiplayer experience. Most of activities require teamplay, I do not think that base constructing or hunt for bosses is really enjoyable in solo, as it turns into heavy grind. In my opinion, a couple of friends is totally required for playing Conan.

So, may I recommend this game? Lets see...
If you want a single-player game - Conan is obviously wrong choice.
If you want a competative PvP game - I think, it is not a good choice.
If you want a cooperative PvE game and have a couple of friends to play with - this is where Conan really shines.

Despite some flaws, I loved this game and enjoyed every single hour I spended in it. And yet again, I must give my deepest thanks for a person who kindly provided us a great server to play.

First, let me say that Conan Exiles is an excellent tribute to Robet E. Howard's Conan Universe. Anyone who is a fan of the Conan movies, books, or games is definitely going to like this one.

IMO Conan Exiles has a lot to offer; beautiful graphics, an interesting backstory (which is revealed through exploration), dungeons, siege warfare, a strong modding community. It posesses some very unique mechanics like climbing and the upcoming sorcery system, as well as a lot more on the way. 

Furthermore, to address a common complaint, the melee combat is a lot like Skyrim at the moment. With simple light and heavy attacks the combat is nothing exraordinary, BUT is going to be revamped very shortly and will feature an in-depth combo attack system. Each weapon type will have its own unique combo sets (yes, multiple combo sets for every weapon type) and effects (cripple, bleed, knockdown, etc.), somewhat like the Age of Conan melee system.

In regard to online play; there are a wide variety of server settings if you want to run your own server (or play single player), similar to what ARK offers. However, there are plenty of private and official servers available to play on. Funcom has a quite a few server types to choose from on their official servers, but it basically boils down to PVP and PVE with varying degrees of roleplaying and XP/resource gain. The player limit on the official servers is 40 people, which is too low to be honest, as people tend to flock to the most crowded servers when the one they were playing on fills up, causing annyoing queue times. 

PVP servers allow the destruction of player buildings, which I think is great. It does take a lot to destroy buildings above tier 1 and if you're good at building and find a decent spot to build in, you won't have to worry about it too much. The truth of it is though, that every PVP server has its share of bastards who will go out of their way to destroy everything they can. If you don't want to deal with that, no big deal, play on a PVE server.

That said, the game does have some bugs, some of which are very annoying. Honestly though, nobody should be surprised by an early access game having bugs. The whole point of early access is to suppliment the developers' budget to finish the game after all.  

Now, Funcom has a history of ruining good games (Age of Conan, Secret World, etc.), but to their credit Conan Exiles has a very hard working team that seems to truly care about creating a quality game and releases regular updates aimed at fixing said bugs, as well as adding a plethora of new content. It really has come a long way since it's early access launch (which wasn't that long ago), especially when compared to games like ARK, which has taken years to get to where it is now (and is still buggy). 

In short, this is a great game which is only going to get better. However, if you can't live with some bugs then do yourself a favor and wait until the game is officially released instead of trash talking it now and making yourself look like an idiot. It saddens me greatly to see such an amazing game slapped with the "mixed reviews" label because of some impatient fools who don't understand the meaning of "early access".

[h1]Conan Exiles[/h1]

First off; this game came out on the 30'th of January. It's gotten plenty of negative reviews even though it's in EA and has literally only been out for a little while. 

I own pretty much every popular survival game out there and went through my phases with them all. DayZ, 7 Days To Die, The Forest, Ark and a few others. This game for just being released definitely seems promising as it surpasses many EA games in performance, playability and existing content. 

That said...

In my experience this game has been great so far. There is some truth to a lot of the negative reviews when it comes to lag. New servers don't seem to lag at all - for me at least. However, when it gets closer to 30+ people and people building structures and leaving it seems to clutter up and start to get a bit jumpy. I haven't experienced such ridiculous lag that it's unplayable as most of these negatives reviews seem to say. I'm running the game on an i7 4790k / 970 / 16GB ram and I've had barely any issues apart from slight rubberbanding at high populations.
[list]
[*] So far I've experienced a great community (I play on RP/PVP servers) - There's a selection to the type of community you want to play with which is very unique and a welcome addition to the server selection menu. 

[*] Similar to Ark, the crafting system is intuitive and if playing on slower settings you'll find yourself immersed for long gaming sessions. It is immersive enough to generally always be doing something such as collecting ores, leather, or even chopping up human corpses for rituals to whatever Gods you serve.

[*] The leveling system is in combination with the crafting system, which makes it give you the urgency to want to and have to level before being able to unlock more effective equipment. Even at this stage of EA there's quite a lot to do - even if it feels a bit grindy at times, you always feel like you're making progress towards something.

[*] The environment... Sandstorms are quite awesome to experience. Footprints in the sand, and ruins of a past civilization are all a sight. I quickly became immersed in the environment after finding journals that give some light to the story, caves filled with exiles and random small bonfires with NPCs. 

[*] Thralls. Thralls are a great addition to this game. You can bash an NPC over the head with a Truncheon, knocking them out, and drag them back to the wheel of pain to break their spirits having them join your cause. You can outfit your base with Thrall archers to defend it while you're offline. Have Dancers, Fighters, Blacksmiths, Carpenters, Armorsmiths - which all benefit you in different ways. I look forward to this feature becoming more refined.

[*] Building. The building is pretty great. I've seen some amazing structures and the amount you can do with the more simpler buildings, like Sandstone which happens to also be quite easy to make, are quite awesome. Building around hills/mountains using stairs. Player buildings quickly become something that seems visually possible and immersive - apart from the occassional completely ridiculous building.

I purchased Conan Exiles when it recently hit v1.0, and have played the game co-op with one friend on a private dedicated server. We had a lot of fun playing the game. Exploring the varied landscape of the world is very nice, the character customization and barbarian-themed armor and weapons are cool, building and decorating is interesting and satisfying, the climbing mechanics are really enjoyable, and it's a beautiful game to look at, too.

Ultimately though, I can't recommend it in its current state. Here's why:

[h1]Combat[/h1]
The combat system, described by some reviewers as feeling nice and fluid, is afflicted by some serious issues, the most serious being shields. A player or NPC can keep his or her shield raised indefinitely, and the shield will totally negate the damage of almost any attack, high or low, with no loss of stamina. This is most obvious (and hilarious) when fighting frost giants. Their gigantic heavy axe attacks with huge windup animations simply stop dead upon contact with a player's shield, as if there's no weight or momentum behind them; you can stand around blocking all of their attacks until the shield eventually breaks, if so desired.

There is no hard counter to shields, whether being used by players or NPCs. You can perform a kick to unbalance your opponent, but they can recover and get the shield back up before you even escape the kick animation lock. You can't force them to drop their shield with heavy combos, since weapons rebound off shields, interrupting combos. You can't outflank them, because they can easily turn to face you, with lock-on in the case of player vs. player. All you can really do is move erratically and flail around like crazy hoping to get lucky hits in: essentially button-mashing. 

In contrast to invincible shields with no counter, bows and ranged weapons come pre-nerfed, do terrible damage, and feature very low projectile velocity and exaggerated ballistic firing arcs, presumably because FunCom couldn't figure out how to balance ranged weapons properly. Fortunately, mods exist to at least un-nerf ranged weapon damage for solo play and on private servers, but unfortunately you'll be stuck with the silly flight physics that resemble throwing a tennis ball more so than firing an arrow.

Other issues with combat include huge quadrupedal bosses and enemies that turn on a dime, very poor telegraphing of some enemy attacks especially if your ping is higher than the single digits, and several other miscellaneous issues. It's also worth noting that boss hit points are massively inflated to be balanced around groups of 10+ players, so for solo and small-scale co-op you'll definitely need a mod.

Finally, you can avoid all combat, even PvP, simply by running away. Just keep on running and you'll be fine. Leopards can't catch you, for example, nor can a pack of wolves. Is an entire 10-man clan after you in PvP? Just run away, you'll be fine. If you think I'm kidding, Google it up, folks. The meta is real.

[h1]Enemy Placement, Creatures, and AI[/h1]
Conan Exiles has a serious problem with mob placement. For starters, enemies always spawn in the exact same spots, just like in an MMO (and also like an MMO, they're mostly there to guard resource nodes). Some wander a bit, but you will always know pretty much exactly where they'll be after you've visited an area one time. This applies to every creature and humanoid in the game. Compare to ARK: You may have a general idea of which dinosaurs are where, but they range over a huge area, and you never really know when or where a carnotaur or pack of allosaurs might appear. Compare to The Forest: Cannibals scout intelligently and patrol large areas unpredictably.

Creatures in Conan Exiles, for the most part, have no real ecosystem simulation (one exception: nest-guarding aggro), and their AI is very simplistic. They just stand around in their always-the-same spawn locations; the aggressive ones charge you headlong to attack when you enter their aggro radius, no matter what. None of them engage in threat displays to warn you off first, for example, as real-life gorillas might do.

Crocodiles are a special case. They stand around on land, charge headlong at their targets instead of laying in ambush, can't swim properly when they do go into the water, and can't even attack you if they're in the water with you. Yes, that's right: [b]The crocodiles in Conan Exiles cannot swim properly or attack you in the water.[/b] Think about that for a second, folks.

Along the same lines, gorillas can't climb anything; big cats also can't climb (yes, a cat that can't climb) and as mentioned earlier, can't even manage to catch/deal damage to a running human. Spiders can't climb, either. Essentially, all NPCs/mobs can only move along the ground, and of the very few that can enter water, there isn't much meaningful they can do there. The big cats do sit around on Pride Rock lookalikes in some areas, though, which is a nice touch.

[h1]Questionable Design Decisions[/h1]
The store page makes a big deal about The Purge, a mechanic in which a horde of enemy NPCs appears to attack your base, but its implementation is extremely disappointing. You don't get to test out defensive walls, traps, palisades, boiling oil, flame orbs, and so on against a horde of enemies outside your gate when The Purge occurs. No, they just spawn anywhere on the foundation blocks of your base and attack your stuff and your thralls. This is exploitable, too, and also can be buggy.

There are no mounts or vehicles of any kind in Conan Exiles. For the most part, you will run or walk everywhere, constantly using up your stamina. For a game clearly in the same genre as ARK et al., this is very silly. I've heard a rumor that the developers claim the game engine "can't handle" fast mounts, and if that rumor is true, that is also silly since Conan Exiles is built with Unreal 4, which can handle vehicles just fine.

There is a limited fast travel device available to discover and build in one of the mid- to high-tier areas of the game, but it is limited to traveling from a huge and expensive placeable teleportation item to one of ten fixed points around the game world, one-way (unless you build more of that huge and expensive item nearby every fixed point).

[h1]General Bugginess[/h1]
Bugs are to be expected in this type of sandbox survival game, but some of the bugs currently present in Conan Exiles are really obnoxious. I pity anyone playing on a server where they don't have access to admin tools to work around bugs and other issues.

I'm not going to make an exhaustive list, but here's a good example: Named thralls (humans you can capture and enslave who have non-generic names) have goofy, super-far-apart alien eyes. Here, I'd better show you:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1392018529

Yep, every single one of them.

Another bug that particularly annoyed us was items (including plot-essential quest items) seeming to vanish from the game files so completely that you can't even spawn them in with admin commands, let alone obtain them normally. This is usually blamed on mods by the community, but also occurs when no mods that touch items in any way are installed, or even with no mods at all.

[h1]In Conclusion[/h1]
This is a fun game, but it's plagued by some serious issues, including some very questionable design decisions that I doubt will ever be overhauled. I don't regret buying it or playing it, but I definitely wouldn't recommend it to any of my Steam friends in its current state. I wouldn't recommend ARK either, mind you, with ARK being the elephant in the current survival sandbox room.

As an early adopter of [b]Conan Exiles[/b], I was excited when it finally got released in early May after a long wait. And even though most of every aspect of the game was vastly improved, my playtime was riddled with game breaking bugs (dumb AI, item duplication, skill points abuse etc), to broken mechanics (decay, unbalanced purge mobs, unresponsive thralls etc) and minor other glitches galore.

But honestly, since my time on Age of Conan (almost a decade ago), I missed the hardcore fantasy theme genre and gave Conan Exiles quite the leeway, expecting most of the problems will eventually be ironed out. Initially hopping official servers due to them being full and after trying some private run servers (which fell foul to admins having their personal vendettas against some players), I decided to start a local server and try the game solo.

And for a while, it was a bliss and all was well with the game, until... 

Finally, here's the reason why I haven't touched Conan Exiles the past few weeks and the reason I will be removing it; the "Red Shell" spyware found in-game. I cannot in all seriousness fathom how Funcom thought it acceptable incorporating 3rd party spyware in their game, especially when GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) was about to become EU law, a mere 2 weeks after the game's release!! And why would anyone bother with spyware that tracks you "outside" your game, like your facebook, twitter, youtube, web etc habits you might ask? After all Red Shell fashions itself as "[...]a means for video game makers to 'uncover' where their players come from through 'reliable attribution'". You would have thought Funcom would at least have learned a small lesson from the Kerbal Space Program's 3rd party "EULA spyware".

Bottom line, I cannot recommend a game or a game maker like Funcom, which thinks this practice is acceptable. To be fair, after they were found out, they removed Red Shell from Conan Exiles but I ask myself, do I trust them anymore? As such, I cannot recommend Conan Exiles or other Funcom games to any of my friends, without a huge red-flag warning for their shady practices.

But if you think the above is water under the bridge and does not apply to you, then please support this developer with your hard-earned cash because you are a better person than me.

Sorry Funcom, you were caught red-handed with spyware and as a top athlete failing their drug test, earning my trust would require a lot more than idle excuses.

I love, love the start of the game. Building up from nothing is just chef's kiss, the dangers feel real and you have to prioritise what you want vs what you need and completing journey steps is very fun to do. Sucks that there's only one save slot, because I'd love to make new characters just to piss around when taking a break from my main save.

But then you get to the middle, where you actually start going off into dungeons and looking for fights and this is where it starts to get less fun. You find legendary weapons, you upgrade your armour as best you can, but some of the fight mechanics are just straight up bullshit even at max level. When I first hit level 60 I thought it was a glitch because that's such a weird number to stop at (most other games cap you at 100) and I felt hopelessly unprepared for even the minibosses like the spiders and the crocodiles and the white tiger. My thralls never survive much past level 11 no matter how careful I try to be (especially with the new update making thralls drawing aggro one of the first skills you learn).

I'm no stranger to games where you need to simply git gud (Dark Souls, Elden Ring) but the combat is just not on par with what the enemies can do to you. Getting stunlocked by 4 skeletons all doing combos at the same time is a miserable experience because there's not really anything you can do except wait for them to finish and hope you didn't die. You can't block with a two handed weapon for some reason and the bosses around the map just seem like damage sponges you have to walk in circles around waiting for your unreasonably minuscule stamina pool to regenerate because dodging, the most useful fight mechanic is also the most expensive. Why is it easier to kill the witch queen, a main sequence boss than it is to kill the spider in the middle of the map, very close to noob river?

I've gotten a bit more serious this past playthrough, but I still feel like some of the later game aspects are poorly balanced, and though they've listened to reviews like mine about the journey size being small, there's still large periods of nothing inbetween excitement. For the dlcs, they're not too pricey but also don't really offer a lot more than building decorations, and I bought siptah just so I could get more options for character customization at the start, the beards look like roadkill. They are now releasing everything on the bazaar which is annoying with the way its a revolving door. 

As of 2026 I'm kind of eesh about all of the new things. Enhanced looks great but doesn't run so good on my current rig. Not supporting the bazaar for legacy is unfortunate and a number of modders have already decided not to upgrade their works so porting existing worlds is out of the question. I use this game primarily to build things in so I will probably be sticking with legacy until performance improves. Appreciate the attempt to optimise the file sizes and everything but more warning would've been great.

TLDR: Start of the game is super fun. Middle can be tedious. Endgame? Play to find out.
